note: Adapted from the species description of Sands (1972); the original is in English and the genus has no soldier caste, only the alate and worker being described; measurement tables, figure numbers, type specimens and distribution records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Comparisons with the other species of group II are mostly given in the descriptions of the species treated above. Distinction from the species of group III rests mainly on the mandibular and enteric characters of the worker and on the reduced third apical spur of the fore tibia. A. irrixosus is larger and its accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible is widely separated from the molar prominence. In A. empodius the meso- and metanotum of the alate are narrower and the apical tooth of the mandibles shorter, while its worker differs in the nearly dorsal, sessile, trilobed enteric valve seating and in the distinct third apical spur of the fore tibia. The abdomen of the worker does dehisce.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish white, pilosity pale yellow, sparse and fine. Postclypeus rather strongly inflated, Pcl/W 0.33, Pcl/Ri 3.05; apical tooth of mandibles rather long, La/Li 0.79, Ra/Ri 1.07; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible just separated from the molar prominence in surface view, compound ratio 15.81; first marginal tooth of the right mandible slightly posterior to the line from the apical to the second marginal tooth, the anterior edges of the marginal teeth about equal in length. Fore tibia hardly inflated, Ti/Tw 4.55, third apical spur reduced, almost lost. Junction of mesenteron and proctodaeum almost transverse and slightly oblique, to the right of the Malpighian nodule; enteric valve seating lateral or slightly ventral in the undissected abdomen, rather distinctly bilobed, connected to the second proctodaeal pouch by a long neck, no spinules detectable on the membranous wall of the valve outside the inner cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule sepia brown, not darkened above the ocelli; fontanelle small, less than half the length of the ocellus, very short-oval, slightly depressed in the middle and faintly striate, pale yellowish brown; mid-spot circular, flat, smaller than the fontanelle, sepia brown; postclypeus brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal mark flat, crescent-shaped, brown; antennae yellowish brown. Pronotum brown, meso- and metanotum yellowish brown, only the metanotum with a transverse dark suture; femora yellowish brown, tibiae paler, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites and dorsal spiracles yellowish brown, sternites and ventral spiracles pale yellowish brown, middle of the sternites yellow; cerci yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule evenly rounded; ocelli medium-sized, separated from the compound eye by slightly less than their own minimum diameter; postclypeus rather weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.25, Pcl/Ra 2.61, posterior margin undulate rather than evenly rounded, median suture distinct. Apical tooth of mandibles rather short, La/Li 0.66, Ra/Rj 0.86; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible just separated from the molar prominence in surface view, compound ratio 10.55; tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible in the same line, the anterior edges of the marginal teeth almost equal, the first slightly longer. Pilosity of head capsule yellowish brown, uneven, not felted. Constriction between meso- and metanotum slightly wide, M/W 0.32. Third apical spur of fore tibia distinct.
